A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ReLaX work. Their complete main texts and supplementary materials, including equations, tables, figures, and algorithms, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original reasoning benchmark evaluations, training dynamics, component ablations, qualitative cases, and runtime measurements in Section 4 and the supplement.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds latent-trajectory visualizations and hyperparameter sensitivity experiments.

M1.justification: The learned and frozen Koopman dictionary, DSD definition, positive-advantage weighting, adaptive KL mechanism, and optimization objective remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 adds backend annotations and explicit log-probability computation, documenting implementation without establishing a new procedure.

E1.justification: Both retain ViRL39K and DAPO-Math-17K/MATH training data, seven multimodal benchmarks, six mathematical benchmarks, and the same qualitative cases. The added model diagnostics and parameter sweeps do not document new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1, 2, and 5 and the multimodal method comparisons. The new DeepSeek-Math visualization is a diagnostic example, not an added competing method; the new citations are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Table 3 changes the reported DSD threshold from 25 to 10; this does not establish that retained experiments were rerun. New diagnostics use DeepSeek-Math-7B and sweep m over 5, 25, 50, 100, 200 and the threshold over 10, 25, 50, infinity. Benchmark splits and decoding metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 extends the existing analyses with t-SNE examples of correct and incorrect latent trajectories (Figure 7) and sensitivity tests for Koopman dimension and DSD threshold (Figure 11). Existing exploration-coefficient and component ablations, runtime analyses, and qualitative cases are retained.

E5.justification: Mean@1 and mean@32 reporting remains unchanged. Neither version documents repeated training runs, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests; the added diagnostic plots introduce no stated uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Tables 1, 2, 5, and 6 retain their numerical results. The DSD traces in v1 Figure 7b are revised in v2 Figure 6b. New results show poor behavior at m=5 and reported collapse around 50 steps without thresholding, alongside new trajectory examples. These are diagnostic additions and revisions, not improved benchmark scores.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 adds an explicit stochastic latent-state formulation, x_t = F(x_{t-1}, omega_t), with omega_t sampled from P_omega (v2 Equation 6). The Koopman approximation, DSD definition, residual formulation, and loss equations are otherwise retained; no new theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain DSD, latent-dynamics regularization through ReLaX, mitigation of premature convergence, and reasoning improvements over token-level approaches. Although the abstract and conclusion are condensed, the introduction retains the state-of-the-art claim across seven multimodal and six text-only benchmarks.

C2.justification: v2 explains how intrinsic dynamics mediate the effect of stochastic sampling and explicitly qualifies that sample-level DSD does not strongly correlate with correctness. The new sensitivity discussion identifies failure conditions at insufficient Koopman dimension and unrestricted DSD, refining the method's applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project repository address and identifies vLLM generation and Transformers log-probability/hidden-state computation in Algorithm 1. Table 3 revises the threshold and removes the previously disclosed minibatch size of 32. Hardware, optimizers, evaluation settings, and runtime figures are retained; repository availability was not independently checked.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Generative Multimodal Models Are In-Context Learners, Show-o2, and Qwen3-Omni around the multimodal motivation. The related-work survey and positioning against token-level exploration methods remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: Substantial portions of the abstract, DSD explanation, ablation and comparative discussions, and conclusion are rewritten or condensed. Contributions are consolidated, the text-only training-dynamics discussion moves to the supplement, and the supplementary overview and qualitative-case ordering are reorganized.

P2.justification: v2 adds two diagnostic figures, revises the DSD panel and its axis range, and relocates the former Figure 4 to supplementary Figure 8. It also rearranges case tables, boxes the supplementary overview, and removes a Table 3 row. Most existing graphics and table designs are retained.

improvement.justification: The new sensitivity experiments address v1's untested choices of Koopman dimension and DSD threshold, while Figure 7 qualifies DSD's relationship to correctness. These modestly strengthen experimental support and interpretation. The gain is limited by removed minibatch information, the unexplained default-threshold revision, and unreconciled DSD traces between v2 Figures 6b and 10; benchmark evidence remains unchanged.
